shared_elements: low-relief carving on a stone surface
registers/columns of repeated units filling the field
stylized human faces/heads (in A's glyph blocks) and human figures (in B)
dense, ordered repetition across the whole surface
justification: The only real correspondence is that both are relief-carved surfaces filled with dense, orderly repeated units — a double column of square glyph blocks in A versus a horizontal file of standing human figures in B — and both include stylized human heads, though in A only as tiny elements inside sign-blocks. B depicts a narrative procession of full-length bearded figures in profile with tall headdresses, robes, and held objects (a bird, a vessel), interacting with smaller attendants, whereas A depicts no scene at all, only a script-like grid of enclosed, cartouche-framed signs; the depicted content, relationships and conventions are essentially unrelated.
